name: Montana
requirementsNote: Montana state law does not mandate renters insurance, but property managers frequently require proof of coverage in standard rental agreements.

demographics.demographicNote: Most Montana renters choose thirty thousand dollars in personal property coverage with a five hundred dollar deductible, a level that fits the state's below average rates while still accounting for real wildfire and hail exposure.

riskFactors.title: Western Montana Wildfire Risk
riskFactors.description: Nearly seventy percent of all recorded wildfires in Montana have occurred since 2000, and roughly twenty nine percent of properties statewide face high wildfire risk, concentrated in the mountainous western half of the state. Fire and smoke damage to personal belongings is covered under a standard renters policy.

riskFactors.title: Eastern Plains Hail
riskFactors.description: Southeastern Montana experiences severe hailstorms with stones reaching golf ball size during peak storm season from May through August, with around twenty damaging hail events recorded in 2025 alone. Hail damage to personal property is covered under a standard renters policy.

riskFactors.title: Western Montana Earthquake Risk
riskFactors.description: Parts of western Montana, particularly areas near the Rocky Mountain Front and Yellowstone region, carry real earthquake risk that many renters overlook. Standard renters insurance excludes earthquake damage, so renters in these areas may want a separate earthquake endorsement.

faqs.question: Is renters insurance required in Montana?
faqs.answer: No. Montana does not legally require renters insurance, though most landlords mandate at least one hundred thousand dollars in liability coverage as part of the lease agreement.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover wildfire damage in Montana?
faqs.answer: Yes. Fire and smoke damage to personal belongings is covered under a standard renters policy, which matters given nearly seventy percent of Montana's recorded wildfires have occurred since 2000.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover hail damage in Montana?
faqs.answer: Yes. Hail damage to personal property is covered under a standard renters policy, especially relevant in southeastern Montana, where golf ball sized hail is common during peak storm season.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover earthquake damage in Montana?
faqs.answer: No. Standard renters insurance excludes earthquake damage, a real though often overlooked risk in western Montana near the Rocky Mountain Front and Yellowstone region.

faqs.question: How much does renters insurance cost in Montana?
faqs.answer: Montana renters insurance runs slightly below the national average, with Bozeman typically the most affordable city and rates varying based on local wildfire and hail exposure. Use the calculator above for a Montana renters insurance quote based on your specific coverage choices.

blogContent.whyThisRate: Montana renters insurance stays slightly below the national average despite the state facing two genuinely significant weather risks on opposite ends of its geography. Western Montana's mountainous terrain has seen nearly seventy percent of the state's recorded wildfires occur since 2000, with roughly twenty nine percent of properties statewide now facing high wildfire risk. Eastern Montana faces an entirely different hazard, severe hailstorms with stones reaching golf ball size that produced around twenty damaging events in 2025 alone. A less known third risk sits in western Montana near the Rocky Mountain Front and Yellowstone region, where real earthquake activity exists but remains excluded from standard coverage. Renters insurance, which covers personal belongings rather than a building's structure, feels less of the wildfire pressure reshaping Montana's homeowners insurance market, keeping the renters insurance base rate close to affordable despite the state's genuinely elevated wildfire risk.
blogContent.howCalculated: For a standard profile, twenty thousand dollars in personal property coverage, one hundred thousand dollars in liability, and a five hundred dollar deductible, our Montana renters insurance calculator applies the state's base rate of one hundred fifty dollars a year with no adjustment at these default levels, landing around one hundred thirty two to one hundred sixty eight dollars a year, or roughly eleven to fourteen dollars a month. Renters in western wildfire prone areas near Missoula or eastern hail prone counties should expect real world quotes to vary from this statewide baseline based on local risk.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Within the West region, Montana's rate sits below Arizona and Colorado despite sharing meaningful wildfire and hail exposure, reflecting the state's overall lower population density and construction replacement costs. Compared to the national average, Montana renters insurance runs slightly more affordable, even as the state's homeowners insurance market faces mounting pressure from wildfire risk that renters insurance itself largely avoids.
